formats.key: permitAndCall(bytes permit, bytes action)
effects: Calls permit on the token in the first 20 bytes of `permit`, which sets an allowance from the signer to the router; the amount comes from the permit data and can be unlimited.
Delegatecalls the router itself with `action`, so the inner swap or fill runs with the signer as msg.sender and with the same msg.value.
Any native value sent with the call is spent by the inner action (for example ethUnoswap or a swap from ETH).
formats.shown: "Execute with permit" and the inner action decoded as a nested screen; the permit (token, spender, amount, deadline) and the native value are hidden.

findings.title: permitAndCall is payable and the inner delegatecall spends msg.value, but no field shows the native value.
findings.evidence: PermitAndCall.permitAndCall: `function permitAndCall(bytes calldata permit, bytes calldata action) external payable` ... `delegatecall(gas(), address(), ptr, action.length, 0, 0)` keeps msg.value. Descriptor permitAndCall fields: only `action` (calldata, calleePath @.to, no amountPath) and `permit` (visible never). No `@.value` field.
findings.fix: Add a field {"path":"@.value","label":"Amount to Send","format":"amount"} and set "amountPath": "@.value" in the calldata params so the nested screen gets the value.

findings.title: permitAndCall hides the permit, which can give the router an unlimited allowance that lasts after the swap.
findings.evidence: tryPermit(token, msg.sender, address(this), permit) in AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol; descriptor `{"label":"Permit","path":"permit","visible":"never"}`. In case 10 the permit value is 0xffff…ffff for cbBTC, which is an unlimited allowance.
findings.fix: Show the permit token (the first 20 bytes of `permit`) as a token field. Change the intent to "Approve router and swap" so the allowance is stated.

findings.title: permitAndCall intent "Execute with permit" does not say that a swap or an order fill runs.
findings.evidence: descriptor permitAndCall `"intent": "Execute with permit"`; the field label says "Swap" even when `action` is a fill or a cancel.
findings.fix: Use the intent "Approve and execute" and label the nested field "Action".

formats.key: swap(address executor, (address srcToken, address dstToken, address srcReceiver, address dstReceiver, uint256 amount, uint256 minReturnAmount, uint256 flags) desc, bytes data)
effects: Takes desc.amount of desc.srcToken from the signer and sends it to desc.srcReceiver; when srcToken is ETH, msg.value must equal desc.amount.
When the _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH flag is set, msg.value can be more than desc.amount (or non-zero for a token source); the executor receives all of it.
Sends at least desc.minReturnAmount of desc.dstToken to desc.dstReceiver, or to the signer when dstReceiver is zero.
With the _PARTIAL_FILL flag, it refunds the unspent source tokens and scales the minimum down in proportion to the amount spent.
formats.shown: "Swap" with the amount to send in srcToken, the minimum to receive in dstToken, and the beneficiary; the executor, srcReceiver, flags, data and msg.value are hidden.

findings.title: swap is payable, and with the extra-ETH flag the native value is more than the amount shown; no field shows it.
findings.evidence: GenericRouter.swap: `if (desc.flags & _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH != 0) { if (msg.value <= (srcETH ? desc.amount : 0)) revert ...}`; _execute forwards `callvalue()` to the executor. Descriptor swap has no `@.value` field and `desc.flags` is visible never.
findings.fix: Add {"path":"@.value","label":"Native value sent","format":"amount"}.

findings.title: swap shows the zero dstReceiver as 0x000…0, but the code then pays the signer.
findings.evidence: GenericRouter.swap: `address payable dstReceiver = (desc.dstReceiver == address(0)) ? payable(msg.sender) : desc.dstReceiver;` Descriptor field desc.dstReceiver uses the beneficiary definition (addressName) and has no senderAddress.
findings.fix: Add "params": {"senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull"} to the desc.dstReceiver field.

findings.title: swap hides the partial-fill flag, which lowers the minimum received in proportion to the amount spent.
findings.evidence: GenericRouter.swap: `if (desc.flags & _PARTIAL_FILL != 0) { ... spentAmount -= unspentAmount; srcToken.uniTransfer(payable(msg.sender), unspentAmount); }`; `desc.flags` is visible never.

findings.title: swap intent "Swap" names no tokens; there is no interpolatedIntent.
findings.evidence: descriptor swap `"intent": "Swap"`.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent: "Swap {desc.amount} for at least {desc.minReturnAmount}".

formats.key: unoswap(uint256 token, uint256 amount, uint256 minReturn, uint256 dex)
effects: Takes `amount` of `token` from the signer and sends it to the pool or the router.
Sends at least `minReturn` of the pool's output token to the signer; when the unwrap flag in `dex` is set, the output is ETH.
formats.shown: "Swap" with the amount to send in the input token, a raw minimum to receive with no token, the signer as beneficiary, and the pool.

findings.title: unoswap shows the minimum to receive as a raw integer; the pool decides the output token.
findings.evidence: descriptor unoswap field `minReturn` uses minReceiveAmount with no tokenPath; case 6 shows "Minimum to Receive: 1099406466248680". The output token comes from the pool in `dex` (ProtocolLib flags, _unoswapV2/V3), not from calldata.
findings.fix: Change the label to "Minimum to receive (raw units)" so nobody reads it as whole tokens.

formats.key: cancelOrder(uint256 makerTraits, bytes32 orderHash)
effects: When makerTraits uses the bit invalidator, it invalidates the signer's nonce from makerTraits; this cancels every order that uses that nonce, and orderHash is ignored.
Otherwise it marks orderHash as fully filled for the signer, which cancels that one order.
formats.shown: "Cancel limit orders" with the order hash in raw form; makerTraits is hidden.

findings.title: cancelOrder shows the order hash, but in bit-invalidator mode the hidden nonce in makerTraits decides what is cancelled.
findings.evidence: cancelOrder: `if (makerTraits.useBitInvalidator()) { _bitInvalidator[msg.sender].massInvalidate(makerTraits.nonceOrEpoch(), 0); } else { _remainingInvalidator[msg.sender][orderHash] = ...fullyFilled(); }`; descriptor `makerTraits` is visible never.
findings.fix: Show the nonce from makerTraits (a byte slice of the nonce/epoch bits) with the label "Nonce (bit-invalidated orders)".

findings.title: cancelOrder shows only the order hash, so the order's assets and amounts are not visible.
findings.evidence: descriptor cancelOrder field `orderHash` format raw.

formats.key: cancelOrders(uint256[] makerTraits, bytes32[] orderHashes)
effects: For each pair, it either invalidates the signer's nonce from makerTraits (bit-invalidator mode) or marks the order hash as fully filled.
formats.shown: "Cancel limit orders" with the list of order hashes in raw form; makerTraits is hidden.

findings.title: cancelOrders shows order hashes, but for bit-invalidator orders the hidden makerTraits nonces decide what is cancelled.
findings.evidence: cancelOrders loops `cancelOrder(makerTraits[i], orderHashes[i])`; cancelOrder ignores orderHash when useBitInvalidator(). Descriptor `makerTraits` is visible never.
findings.fix: Show the nonce slice of `makerTraits.[]` next to `orderHashes.[]`.

findings.title: cancelOrders shows only order hashes, so the terms of each order are not visible.
findings.evidence: descriptor cancelOrders field `orderHashes.[]` format raw.

formats.key: increaseEpoch(uint96 series)
effects: Increases the signer's epoch for one `series` by 1. This cancels only the signer's epoch-checked orders in that series; bit-invalidator orders and orders in other series stay fillable.
formats.shown: "Cancel all limit orders" with the signer's address as "Orders maker"; the series is hidden.

findings.title: increaseEpoch says "Cancel all limit orders" but cancels only epoch-checked orders of one hidden series.
findings.evidence: advanceEpoch: `uint256 key = uint160(msg.sender) | (uint256(series) << 160); _epochs[key] = _epochs[key] + amount;` _fill checks the epoch only when `order.makerTraits.needCheckEpochManager()`. Descriptor `"intent": "Cancel all limit orders"`, `series` visible never.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Cancel orders of one series" and show `series` with the label "Order series".

findings.title: increaseEpoch shows the signer's own address in raw form, which tells the signer nothing.
findings.evidence: descriptor increaseEpoch field `@.from` label "Orders maker" format raw.
findings.fix: Replace the field with `series`.

formats.key: fillContractOrder((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits)
effects: When the maker-amount flag (takerTraits bit 255) is not set, the signer sends `amount` (or less) of takerAsset to the order receiver and receives makerAsset in proportion.
When the maker-amount flag is set, `amount` is the makerAsset amount the signer receives, and the signer sends the computed takingAmount of takerAsset, limited only by the hidden threshold.
With the unwrap flag and a WETH maker asset, the signer receives ETH instead of WETH.
formats.shown: "Fill order" with the order's total taking and making amounts, "Amount to sell" always in takerAsset, and an enum for the first byte of takerTraits.

findings.title: fillContractOrder shows `amount` as takerAsset to sell, but with the maker-amount flag it is makerAsset to receive.
findings.evidence: _fill: `if (takerTraits.isMakingAmount()) { makingAmount = Math.min(amount, remainingMakingAmount); takingAmount = order.calculateTakingAmount(...)`; descriptor field `amount` uses fillAmount ("Amount to sell") with `"tokenPath": "order.takerAsset"`; the takerTraits enum has no key for 128 or higher.
findings.fix: Add enum keys for values with bit 0x80 ("Exact amount to receive") and add a second amount field with tokenPath order.makerAsset, or a label that names both modes.

findings.title: fillContractOrder hides the threshold that limits what the signer pays or receives.
findings.evidence: _fill: `uint256 threshold = takerTraits.threshold(); if (takingAmount > threshold) revert TakingAmountTooHigh();` / `if (makingAmount < threshold) revert MakingAmountTooLow();`; descriptor shows only `takerTraits.[:1]`.
findings.fix: Add a field for the threshold slice `takerTraits.[9:]` with the label "Max to pay / min to receive".

findings.title: fillContractOrder labels "Order selling amount" and "Order purchasing amt" read backward from the maker's side.
findings.evidence: definitions takingAmount label "Order selling amount" (order.takerAsset), makingAmount label "Order purchasing amt" (order.makerAsset); case 7 shows "Order selling amount 0.1 WETH", which the order buys.
findings.fix: Use "You pay (order total)" for takingAmount and "You receive (order total)" for makingAmount.

findings.title: fillContractOrder intent "Fill order" names neither asset nor direction.
findings.evidence: descriptor `"intent": "Fill order"`.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent: "Pay {amount} to fill order for {order.makingAmount}".

formats.key: fillContractOrderArgs((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits, bytes args)
effects: Sends takerAsset from the signer to the order receiver and sends makerAsset to `target`; target is the signer, or the first 20 bytes of `args` when the takerTraits target flag is set.
Amounts come from the order extension in `args` (dynamic getters) and are limited only by the hidden threshold.
Calls the taker interaction contract given in `args`.
`amount` is the takerAsset amount or, with the maker-amount flag, the makerAsset amount.
formats.shown: "Fill order" with the order totals, "Amount to sell" in takerAsset and an enum for the first byte of takerTraits; args, which hold the receiver, extension and interaction, are hidden.

findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs hides the target from `args` that receives the signer's purchased makerAsset.
findings.evidence: _parseArgs: `if (takerTraits.argsHasTarget()) { target = address(bytes20(args)); ...}`; _fill sends makerAsset to `receiver = needUnwrap ? address(this) : target`. Descriptor `args` is visible never; the enum has no key for flag 0x08.
findings.fix: Add a field for the target (the first 20 bytes of args, when bit 0x08 of takerTraits is set) labelled "Recipient".

findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs shows `amount` in takerAsset even when the maker-amount flag makes it makerAsset.
findings.evidence: _fill `takerTraits.isMakingAmount()` branch; descriptor `amount` tokenPath `order.takerAsset`, label "Amount to sell".
findings.fix: Add enum keys for bit 0x80 and show the amount in the right token for each mode.

findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs hides the threshold, the only limit on dynamic extension pricing.
findings.evidence: _fill threshold checks (TakingAmountTooHigh / MakingAmountTooLow); the extension from args sets calculateTakingAmount/calculateMakingAmount. Descriptor shows only `takerTraits.[:1]`.
findings.fix: Show `takerTraits.[9:]` as "Max to pay / min to receive".

findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs uses the same backward "Order selling/purchasing" labels.
findings.evidence: definitions takingAmount "Order selling amount", makingAmount "Order purchasing amt".
findings.fix: Use "You pay (order total)" and "You receive (order total)".

formats.key: fillOrder((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes32 r, bytes32 vs, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits)
effects: Sends takerAsset from the signer to the order receiver; when takerAsset is WETH and msg.value > 0, the signer pays ETH instead and gets any excess back.

findings.title: fillOrder labels the WETH the signer receives as "Order purchasing amt" while Unwrap sends ETH.
findings.evidence: case 11: "Order purchasing amt 0.001450069633901244 WETH", "Additional action: Unwrap"; _fill `_WETH.safeWithdrawTo(makingAmount, target)`.
findings.fix: Use "You receive (order total)" and the enum label "Receive as ETH".

findings.format: permitAndCall(bytes permit, bytes action)
findings.title: permitAndCall is payable and the inner delegatecall spends msg.value, but no field shows the native value.
findings.reason: permitAndCall is payable and delegatecalls to itself, so msg.value stays live for the inner call (for example ethUnoswap, or swap with ETH). The outer screen has no @.value field. The calldata field has no amountPath, so the nested screen cannot resolve @.value either.
findings.quote: PermitAndCall.permitAndCall: `function permitAndCall(bytes calldata permit, bytes calldata action) external payable` ... `delegatecall(gas(), address(), ptr, action.length, 0, 0)`; descriptor field `action`: `"format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "@.to"}` (no amountPath)

findings.format: swap(address executor, (address srcToken, address dstToken, address srcReceiver, address dstReceiver, uint256 amount, uint256 minReturnAmount, uint256 flags) desc, bytes data)
findings.title: swap is payable, and with the extra-ETH flag the native value is more than the amount shown; no field shows it.
findings.reason: With the _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH flag, msg.value must be more than desc.amount (or more than 0 for a token source), and _execute forwards all of callvalue() to the executor. The screen shows only desc.amount; desc.flags is visible never and there is no @.value field.
findings.quote: GenericRouter.swap: `if (desc.flags & _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH != 0) { if (msg.value <= (srcETH ? desc.amount : 0)) revert ...}`; _execute: `call(gas(), executor, callvalue(), ...)`; descriptor: `{"label": "Desc Flags", "path": "desc.flags", "visible": "never"}`

findings.format: increaseEpoch(uint96 series)
findings.title: increaseEpoch says "Cancel all limit orders" but cancels only epoch-checked orders of one hidden series.
findings.reason: Reversing my first reading. The finding is right that only one series' epoch-checked orders are cancelled, not all orders. But the severity guide treats a wrong intent label as a warning, and the same wording would also apply to fully cancelling the sender's orders for one series. So this is not critical.
findings.quote: OrderMixin.advanceEpoch: `uint256 key = uint160(msg.sender) | (uint256(series) << 160); _epochs[key] = newEpoch;` / _fill: `if (order.makerTraits.needCheckEpochManager()) {...}`; descriptor: `"intent": "Cancel all limit orders"`, `series` visible never

findings.format: fillContractOrder((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits)
findings.title: fillContractOrder shows `amount` as takerAsset to sell, but with the maker-amount flag it is makerAsset to receive.
findings.reason: With bit 255 of takerTraits set, amount is the makerAsset amount the signer receives, and the signer pays a computed takingAmount. The screen shows amount as 'Amount to sell' in order.takerAsset. The enum has no key for 128 or higher, so the mode is never stated.
findings.quote: _fill: `if (takerTraits.isMakingAmount()) { makingAmount = Math.min(amount, remainingMakingAmount); takingAmount = order.calculateTakingAmount(...)`; TakerTraitsLib `_MAKER_AMOUNT_FLAG = 1 << 255`; descriptor fillContractOrder `amount` `$ref fillAmount` ("Amount to sell"), `"tokenPath": "order.takerAsset"`

findings.format: fillContractOrder((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits)
findings.title: fillContractOrder hides the threshold that limits what the signer pays or receives.
findings.reason: fillContractOrder always passes an empty extension, so both amounts are a linear proportion of order.makingAmount and order.takingAmount, which are on screen. The hidden threshold only adds a revert condition and changes no asset movement.
findings.quote: fillContractOrder: `_fillContractOrder(order, signature, amount, takerTraits, msg.sender, msg.data[:0], msg.data[:0])`; calculateTakingAmount: `if (data.length == 0) { // Linear proportion return AmountCalculatorLib.getTakingAmount(order.makingAmount, order.takingAmount, requestedMakingAmount); }`

findings.format: fillContractOrderArgs((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits, bytes args)
findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs hides the target from `args` that receives the signer's purchased makerAsset.
findings.reason: When the _ARGS_HAS_TARGET bit is set, the first 20 bytes of args become the target, and _fill sends the makerAsset (or the unwrapped ETH) to that target. args is visible never, and the enum has no key with bit 8, so the recipient is never shown.
findings.quote: _parseArgs: `if (takerTraits.argsHasTarget()) { target = address(bytes20(args)); ...} else { target = msg.sender; }`; _fill: `address receiver = needUnwrap ? address(this) : target;`; descriptor: `{"label": "Args", "path": "args", "visible": "never"}`

findings.format: fillContractOrderArgs((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits, bytes args)
findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs shows `amount` in takerAsset even when the maker-amount flag makes it makerAsset.
findings.reason: This is the same isMakingAmount branch as finding 3. The amount is a makerAsset amount, but the screen shows it as 'Amount to sell' in takerAsset.
findings.quote: _fill: `if (takerTraits.isMakingAmount()) { makingAmount = Math.min(amount, remainingMakingAmount); ...`; descriptor fillContractOrderArgs `amount` `"tokenPath": "order.takerAsset"`, label "Amount to sell"

findings.title: fillContractOrderArgs hides the threshold, the only limit on dynamic extension pricing.
findings.reason: With an extension from args, an amount getter chosen by the maker prices the fill. The hidden threshold is then the only limit on what the signer pays (maker-amount mode) or the minimum the signer receives. The screen shows only takerTraits.[:1], so the threshold is never shown.

findings.format: clipperSwap(address clipperExchange, uint256 srcToken, address dstToken, uint256 inputAmount, uint256 outputAmount, uint256 goodUntil, bytes32 r, bytes32 vs)
findings.title: clipperSwap is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: clipperSwap calls clipperSwapTo, which requires msg.value == inputAmount when srcToken is ETH (address 0) and msg.value == 0 otherwise. inputAmount is on screen with tokenPath srcToken.[-20:], and nativeCurrencyAddress includes the zero address.
findings.quote: clipperSwapTo: `if (srcToken_ == _ETH) { if (msg.value != inputAmount) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue(); } else { if (msg.value != 0) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue();`; descriptor `inputAmount` `sendAmount` with `nativeCurrencyAddress` [addressAsEth, addressAsNull]

findings.title: clipperSwapTo is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)

findings.format: permitAndCall(bytes permit, bytes action)
findings.title: permitAndCall is payable and the inner delegatecall spends msg.value, but no field shows the native value.
findings.reason: The delegatecall preserves native value, and an inner swap with the extra-ETH flag forwards it to the executor. Neither the wrapper nor that swap displays this extra value.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, PermitAndCall.permitAndCall: `let success := delegatecall(gas(), address(), ptr, action.length, 0, 0)`; GenericRouter._execute: `call(gas(), executor, callvalue(), ptr, add(0x44, data.length), 0, 0x20)`. descriptor.json, permitAndCall: `"path": "action", "label": "Swap", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "@.to"}`; its only other field is `"path": "permit", "visible": "never"`.

findings.format: swap(address executor, (address srcToken, address dstToken, address srcReceiver, address dstReceiver, uint256 amount, uint256 minReturnAmount, uint256 flags) desc, bytes data)
findings.title: swap is payable, and with the extra-ETH flag the native value is more than the amount shown; no field shows it.
findings.reason: The extra-ETH branch accepts native value beyond the displayed source amount and forwards all of it. The descriptor hides the flag and omits native value.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, GenericRouter.swap: `if (desc.flags & _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH != 0) { if (msg.value <= (srcETH ? desc.amount : 0)) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue(); }`; _execute: `call(gas(), executor, callvalue(), ptr, add(0x44, data.length), 0, 0x20)`. descriptor.json, swap: `"path": "desc.amount", "$ref": "$.display.definitions.sendAmount"` and `"path": "desc.flags", "visible": "never"`; no `@.value` field.

findings.format: increaseEpoch(uint96 series)
findings.title: increaseEpoch says "Cancel all limit orders" but cancels only epoch-checked orders of one hidden series.
findings.reason: The function invalidates epoch-checked orders within one series, leaving other orders executable. The screen promises cancellation of all limit orders and hides that series.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, SeriesEpochManager.advanceEpoch: `uint256 key = uint160(msg.sender) | (uint256(series) << 160);` and `_epochs[key] = newEpoch;`; OrderMixin._fill: `if (order.makerTraits.needCheckEpochManager())` guards `epochEquals(order.maker.get(), order.makerTraits.series(), order.makerTraits.nonceOrEpoch())`. descriptor.json, increaseEpoch: `"intent": "Cancel all limit orders"`, `"path": "series", "visible": "never"`.

findings.title: fillContractOrder shows `amount` as takerAsset to sell, but with the maker-amount flag it is makerAsset to receive.
findings.reason: In maker-amount mode, amount specifies purchased makerAsset rather than sold takerAsset. Displaying the full order's amounts does not correct the fill amount's wrong asset and direction.

findings.format: fillContractOrder((uint256 salt, uint256 maker, uint256 receiver, uint256 makerAsset, uint256 takerAsset, uint256 makingAmount, uint256 takingAmount, uint256 makerTraits) order, bytes signature, uint256 amount, uint256 takerTraits)
findings.title: fillContractOrder hides the threshold that limits what the signer pays or receives.
findings.reason: This entry point supplies an empty extension, so execution prices come from the two displayed order amounts. The omitted threshold adds a rejection condition; it does not authorize a different execution price, making this omission noncritical.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, OrderMixin.fillContractOrder: `return _fillContractOrder(order, signature, amount, takerTraits, msg.sender, msg.data[:0], msg.data[:0]);`; OrderLib.calculateTakingAmount: `return AmountCalculatorLib.getTakingAmount(order.makingAmount, order.takingAmount, requestedMakingAmount);`. descriptor.json, fillContractOrder displays `order.takingAmount` and `order.makingAmount` with `"visible": "always"`. Severity guide, <not_critical> 2: `A value that is shown through another field`.

findings.title: fillOrderArgs hides the threshold, the only limit on dynamic extension pricing.
findings.reason: The extension permits pricing that is not determined by the displayed order amounts. The payment or receipt threshold is omitted because only the first byte of takerTraits is displayed.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, OrderLib.calculateMakingAmount: `return IAmountGetter(address(bytes20(data))).getMakingAmount(`; OrderMixin._fill: `if (takingAmount > threshold) revert TakingAmountTooHigh();` and `if (makingAmount < threshold) revert MakingAmountTooLow();`. descriptor.json, fillOrderArgs: `"path": "takerTraits.[:1]"` and `"path": "args", "visible": "never"`; no threshold field.

findings.format: clipperSwap(address clipperExchange, uint256 srcToken, address dstToken, uint256 inputAmount, uint256 outputAmount, uint256 goodUntil, bytes32 r, bytes32 vs)
findings.title: clipperSwap is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: clipperSwap delegates to clipperSwapTo, which requires native value to equal the displayed inputAmount for ETH swaps. All other inputs reject nonzero native value.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, ClipperRouter.clipperSwap: `return clipperSwapTo(clipperExchange, payable(msg.sender), srcToken, dstToken, inputAmount, outputAmount, goodUntil, r, vs);`; clipperSwapTo: `if (srcToken_ == _ETH) { if (msg.value != inputAmount) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue(); } else { if (msg.value != 0) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue();`. descriptor.json, clipperSwap displays `inputAmount` using sendAmount, `"tokenPath": "srcToken.[-20:]"`, and the native-currency address mapping.

findings.format: clipperSwapTo(address clipperExchange, address recipient, uint256 srcToken, address dstToken, uint256 inputAmount, uint256 outputAmount, uint256 goodUntil, bytes32 r, bytes32 vs)
findings.title: clipperSwapTo is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: The displayed inputAmount already states the ETH sent, enforced by an equality check. Non-ETH swaps reject native value, so a separate @.value field is unnecessary for this claim.
findings.quote: AggregationRouterV6.mainnet.sol, ClipperRouter.clipperSwapTo: `if (srcToken_ == _ETH) { if (msg.value != inputAmount) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue(); } else { if (msg.value != 0) revert RouterErrors.InvalidMsgValue();`. descriptor.json, clipperSwapTo: `"path": "inputAmount", "$ref": "$.display.definitions.sendAmount", "params": {"tokenPath": "srcToken.[-20:]"}`; sendAmount is labeled `"Amount to Send"` and includes `nativeCurrencyAddress`.
